title: Anheuser-Busch Delivered 39,000+ Cans of Emergency Drinking Water Following Flooding in the Southeast U.S.
summary: Anheuser-Busch Delivered 39,000+ Cans of Emergency Drinking Water Following Flooding in the Southeast U.S.
body_markdown:
**Key Facts:**


- ·


39,000+ cans of emergency drinking water delivered to Florida and Tennessee communities impacted by flooding
- ·


Emergency drinking water produced at Anheuser-Busch's Cartersville Brewery
- ·


Anheuser-Busch and its wholesaler partners have donated more than 100 million cans of emergency drinking water since 1988


**November 13, 2026 – St. Louis, MO –** Anheuser-Busch delivered more than 39,000 cans of emergency drinking water to Florida and Tennessee to support residents and first responders as the communities recover from severe flooding.


The donations of emergency drinking water were shipped to Anheuser-Busch wholesaler partners Carroll Distributing of Melbourne, Florida and Tarver Distributing of Charleston, Tennessee, whose teams partnered with local officials and disaster response programs to distribute water to their local community members.


The over 39,000 cans of water were sourced from Anheuser-Busch's brewery in Cartersville, Georgia, which alongside the brewery in Fort Collins, Colorado, periodically pauses beer production to can emergency drinking water and help communities in times of disaster.


**14,000+ Cans of Emergency Drinking Water to Melbourne, Florida**


Anheuser-Busch and its wholesaler partner, Carroll Distributing of Melbourne, Florida, delivered more than 14,000 cans of emergency drinking water to the Melbourne community.


Justin Saenz, Vice President of Carroll Distributing, said: “Supporting our neighbors in a time of need is what community is all about. We’re proud to join Anheuser-Busch, local relief teams, and first responders in supplying clean drinking water as Melbourne residents recover from severe flooding.”


**25,000+ Cans of Emergency Drinking Water to Southeastern Tennessee**


Anheuser-Busch and its wholesaler partner, Tarver Distributing of Charleston, Tennessee, delivered more than 25,000 cans of emergency drinking water to Polk County and surrounding areas.


Ross Tarver, President of Tarver Distributing, said: “Tarver Distributing is proud to partner with Anheuser-Busch to provide emergency drinking water to our community. As our neighbors begin to recover from the flooding, we’re thankful for our community’s first responders, local relief organizations, and Anheuser-Busch for coming together to provide this essential support.”


Anheuser-Busch has a longstanding tradition of providing support for disaster relief efforts. Since the inception of the emergency drinking water program in 1988, Anheuser-Busch and its wholesaler partners have donated more than 100 million cans of clean, safe drinking water to U.S. communities and volunteer fire departments in support of ongoing disaster relief and preparedness efforts.
